correctness.rationale: The factorization of the six-neighbour symbol, exact local group-algebra primary decomposition, root-set inclusion-exclusion, each nilpotency index including the repeated central root, and dyadic penultimate ideal ranks provide an all-size proof. Exact binary Gaussian elimination verified 256 size pairs, 102,912 direct labelled states and nine penultimate ranks. The tests are corroboration, not a substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The arXiv full text of Zaidenberg (2006) provides convolution/Fourier machinery and examples, but not the exact triangular six-neighbour symbol classification, local central nilpotence or sharp last-step rank. The inspected four-page Uguz–Siap–Akin (2013) full text works with ternary-field periodic hexagonal automata and reversible matrices; Bhavadharani–Christy (2025) uses ternary Moore neighbourhoods with null boundaries. The earlier four-neighbour square-grid parity recurrence uses a distinct symbol and does not imply this six-neighbour claim. published-finding corpus targeted searches returned no exact or stronger triangular-torus finding. The 2011 hexagonal paper remains a stated full-text access risk.
residual_risks: A full-text check of the plausibly relevant 2011 Siap–Akin–Uguz hexagonal-automata paper was unavailable (the discoverable abstract concerns reversibility); some unindexed same-operator result could exist. The 2013 follow-on was fully inspected and works over a different finite field.
An unindexed or otherwise inaccessible equivalent classification cannot be excluded by search alone.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family of six-regular triangular lattice quotients has a complete arithmetic attractor/extinction classification: an odd-part gcd controls recurrent dimension, powers of two control exact transient depth, and square versus rectangular dyadic geometry changes sharp last-step rank from 3m/2 to n-2m+2. Global extinction even on arbitrarily large such graphs and exact worst-case proportions supply structural dynamical information beyond a routine finite enumeration.
